comparison: Strong agreement on layer 5 IT cells showing differential responses to closed-loop vs open-loop conditions (C4, C30-C31, C37-C38, C45, C47-C48). Both evaluations rate these findings as SUPPORTED and describe them as robust with appropriate controls.

Perfect agreement on claims C9, C100-C102 regarding antipsychotics reducing propagation of prediction errors to higher visual areas. Both evaluations find the data SUPPORTED, though peer reviewer notes the mechanism is plausible and provides basis for further studies.

Strong agreement on widefield imaging methodology claims (C103-C108, C110-C111). Both evaluations are SUPPORTED and acknowledge the technique's limitations while finding the authors' controls adequate to address hemodynamic artifacts.

Agreement on antipsychotics reducing long-range correlations (C6-C8, C83, C86-C87, C94-C96). Both evaluations are SUPPORTED and describe results as robust. OpenEval includes additional claims about controls and layer specificity not explicitly mentioned by peer reviewer.

Agreement on L5 IT cells showing decreased responses to visual gratings and opposing responses to prediction errors (C63-C65). Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. Peer reviewer also includes interpretation claims C163-C164 about internal representation neurons, which OpenEval addresses separately in R4 and R21.

Agreement on validation of widefield imaging with two-photon data (C43-C44). Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. Peer reviewer finds it 'reassuring' and OpenEval notes qualitative similarity of key findings across modalities. Peer reviewer also includes C79, C90 which OpenEval addresses in R5 and R7.

Partial agreement on antipsychotic effects on L5 IT cells (C73-C74, C80). Both evaluations are SUPPORTED and describe results as robust. OpenEval includes broader set of claims (C71-C80) covering additional controls and convergent evidence from multiple imaging modalities.

Agreement on negative controls for hemodynamic artifacts and injection stress (C88-C89). Both evaluations are SUPPORTED and find these controls reassuring. OpenEval includes additional claims about spatial resolution and layer specificity (C90-C93) that peer reviewer addresses separately.

Divergent evaluations on Cux2 comparison data (C92-C93). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, finding layer specificity well-demonstrated. Peer reviewer rates as UNCERTAIN due to small sample size and recommends cautious interpretation.

Agreement on uncertainty regarding internal representation neuron interpretation (C66-C68). Both evaluations rate as UNCERTAIN and note the speculation. OpenEval emphasizes need for additional experiments while peer reviewer describes it as 'rather speculative.'

Divergent evaluations on overarching conclusion about antipsychotic mechanism (C10). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED by convergent evidence. Peer reviewer rates as UNCERTAIN, describing interpretation as 'more speculative' requiring further validation. Also includes C98 which OpenEval addresses in R8.

Partial overlap on antipsychotic specificity claims. OpenEval rates C95-C98 as SUPPORTED with reasonable speculation. Peer reviewer rates C10, C98 as UNCERTAIN, noting interpretation is speculative but results are robust.

Agreement on uncertainty regarding internal representation neuron interpretation (C163-C164, C166). Both evaluations rate as UNCERTAIN and acknowledge speculation. OpenEval emphasizes functional identity requires further testing; peer reviewer notes it's 'rather speculative.'

Agreement on control experiments ruling out confounds (C39). Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval includes additional claims about nonlinear integration (C40-C41) not explicitly mentioned by peer reviewer.

OpenEval finds correlation data from Figure 2 (C49-C59) SUPPORTED with clear regional and condition-dependent differences. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific correlation analysis claims.
OpenEval rates claims about lateral vs vertical coupling strength (C137-C140) as UNCERTAIN, noting speculation and need for additional experiments. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval rates generalization to other deep layer neuron types (C116-C121) as UNCERTAIN due to explicit speculation and noisy Ntsr1 recordings. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, though peer reviewer notes small sample sizes for Ntsr1 mice elsewhere.
OpenEval rates claims about Tlx3 line specificity (C122-C123) as UNCERTAIN, noting limitation cannot be entirely ruled out. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
OpenEval rates claims about striatal contributions (C130-C134) as SUPPORTED with sound logic but indirect evidence. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
OpenEval rates translational claims about human fMRI (C135-C136) as UNCERTAIN, noting explicit speculation requiring validation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
OpenEval rates conceptual framework and literature context claims (C1-C3, C11-C27) as SUPPORTED by appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background claims.

OpenEval rates synthesis with schizophrenia clinical literature (C141-C157) as SUPPORTED with appropriate citations and reasonable speculative connections. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

Peer reviewer finds L5 IT cells showing decreased responses to visual gratings (C63-C65, C163-C164) SUPPORTED and robust. OpenEval addresses C63-C65 in R3 (SUPPORTED) and C163-C164 in R21 (UNCERTAIN), treating data and interpretation separately.

Peer reviewer finds antipsychotic enhancement of L5 IT locomotion responses (C5, C73-C74, C80) SUPPORTED with robust data but more speculative interpretation. OpenEval addresses these claims in R5 (SUPPORTED) but does not include C5 in that result.
